author: zsfelfoldi
content: <@&836981603216654336> <@&688101493978562687> <@&652918665943056397> <@&1070471163219824730> if you have any further input on the EIP-8304  CFI/DFI decision then please signal it before ACDE so that we can make the decision more efficiently (or postpone it if you are open for further discussion but need more time/info to decide). From my part I already wrote down my thoughts about why this data structure could open up scalability possibilities in the near future, though the most important argument for putting it in Hegota is still the trustless accessibility of an important part of Ethereum which I feel we are kind of obliged to care about even if users are currently happy with trusted indexers (changing this is a key part of our mission and kind of the whole point of Ethereum). After all, EF even made many of us sign a mandate to uphold CROPS values 🙂

author: nixo.eth
content:
Ahead of [this Thursday's ACDE](<https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2223>), I wanted to post a heads up on the Hegotá PFIs we're most likely to discuss. There were two groups: ones that were punted from the last call and the highest client-rated ones as CFI candidates.

**Punted from the last call**:
[8304](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8304/>): Trustless log and transaction index 
  \\\ this one was pending some async discussion with Besu & Reth. Without changes to those positions, default to DFI
[7979](<https://forkcast.org/eips/7979/>): Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM 
  \\\ default to DFI but we wanted compiler teams to come to this upcoming call to weigh in (Solidity & Vyper confirmed to be coming to the call)
[8163](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8163/>): Reserve `EXTENSION (0xae)` opcode 
  \\\ default to DFI but needed weigh-in from other EVM chains, which they did [here](<https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8163-reserve-extension-0xae-opcode/27756/8>) and [here](<https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2223#issuecomment-5719895334>). Notably a small ask / no-op for L1
[8360](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8360/>): TCREATE Opcode 
  \\\ no explicit champion but two have since volunteered and will give an update at the call about the EIP's necessity, status, and any dependencies. Discussion in <#1546549848763932742>. Recent addition to Forkcast (not on rank) because the original proposer didn't bring it to ACD

**Highest client rated EIPs** - please be ready to flag any concerns as these are our "easy CFI" candidates:
[7906](<https://forkcast.org/eips/7906/>): Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
[8250](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8250/>): Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
[8272](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8272/>): Recent Roots for Frame Transactions
[7668](<https://forkcast.org/eips/7668/>): Remove bloom filters
[8253](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8253/>): Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
[3298](<https://forkcast.org/eips/3298/>): Remove storage-clear refund and refund cap
[8131](<https://forkcast.org/eips/8131/>): Unified Transaction Content Floor
